document_metadata.document_title: Stormwater Management Manual for Western Washington (Ecology 2024; city MS4)

design_criteria.water_quality_volume_method: Adopts Ecology Stormwater Management Manual for Western Washington (SWMMWW) Minimum Requirements including runoff treatment and flow control. Local drainage manuals/ordinances typically supplement SWMMWW for city conditions; continuous simulation (WWHM/HSPF) sizes flow control.

evidence.excerpt: City of Olympia MS4 follows Ecology SWMMWW
Document that the maximum ponded depth from the infiltration BMP can infiltrate through the infiltration BMP surface within 48 hours.
evidence.page_or_section: Volume V - Chapter 5 - Page 823 (SSC-4 Drawdown Time)

evidence.excerpt: In most cases, UIC wells are designed to completely drain ponded runoff within 48 to 72 hours after flow to the UIC well has stopped.
The "Default" and "Custom" BSM depth must be 18 inches to provide Runoff Treatment and good growing conditions for selected plants.
The minimum vertical separation is 5 feet between the base of a UIC well and the highest elevation between the seasonal high groundwater table, bedrock, hardpan, or other low-permeability layer.

The base of BMP T7.10: Infiltration Ponds or BMP T7.20: Infiltration Trenches shall be ≥ 5 feet above the seasonal high-water mark, bedrock (or hardpan) or other low permeability layer. A separation down to 3 feet may be considered
If the high water table extends to within five (5) feet of the bottom of an infiltration BMP, the site is seldom suitable.

Where the minimum vertical separation of 1 foot to the seasonal high water table, bedrock, or other impervious layer would not be achieved below bioretention that would serve a drainage area that is less than:
greater than 3 feet below the bottom of BMP T7.30: Bioretention, or greater than 1 foot below the bottom of the lowest gravel base course of BMP T5.15: Permeable Pavement
They are not generally appropriate for sites that have a design infiltration rate less than 0.3 inches per hour.
Design (long-term) infiltration rates up to 3 in/hr can also be considered
Use an initial saturated hydraulic conductivity (Ksat) for the Bioretention Soil Mix (BSM) of 12 in/hr.
Deep ponds (greater than 8 feet) may stratify during summer
biofiltration swales are usually situated on sites with slopes of less than 6%
Minimum slope = 1% to 2% to allow for surface overflow in extreme rainfall
The permeable pavement design includes a 6" layer of sand that meets the size gradation (by weight) given in Table V-7.1: Sand Medium Specification.
biological treatment method, such as a biofiltration swale or constructed wetland.
runoff from these types of landscaped areas should be directed to bioretention, biofiltration, or constructed wetland BMPs prior to discharge to UIC wells.

extraction_quality.review_notes: Municipality coverage via Ecology SWMMWW (Vancouver/Bellevue western WA pattern). Prefer city drainage manual if a durable public PDF is later found.

design_parameters.enrich_notes: Excerpts are Ecology SWMMWW (2024), adopted for Olympia MS4 context. Seasonal high groundwater separation varies by BMP and drainage area (e.g. 1 ft rain garden/small bioretention/permeable base, 3 ft larger bioretention, 5 ft infiltration ponds/trenches and UIC presumptive, 3 ft UIC/alternate infiltration with analysis). Infiltration drawdown check is 48 h; UIC wells cite 48–72 h pond drain. BSM default/custom treatment media depth is 18 in; BSM end-of-life design Ksat uses 12 in/hr (not a single native-soil design rate in these excerpts). Permeable pavement treatment sand layers are 6 in (basic) and 12 in (basic + metals); minimum surface slope 1–2%.
